primitives.name: Catcher Ball Return Strategy
primitives.verbatim_quote: 254 WALTER CAMP'S BOOK OF COLLEGE SPORTS ner, is good policy; but simply to return the ball to the pitcher by way of first or third is inviting the accident of a misplay which will give a runner a base and perhaps a run.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P_m': 'probability of misfire', 'R_b': 'runner advancement base', 'T_p': 'throw to pitcher'}
primitives.assumptions: Throwing to first or third increases P_m due to longer path and potential for error.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When P_m > 0.3, runner advancement occurs with high frequency.

layer2.mapping: Catchers' throwing decisions modeled as stochastic actions minimizing expected runner advancement under error constraints.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of misplays and runner advancement post-error.

primitives.name: Outfield Coverage Efficiency
primitives.verbatim_quote: OUT-FIELDERS THE importance of a strong out-field can hardly be overestimated.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'E_g': 'ground ball error rate', 'C_o': 'coverage effectiveness', 'B_s': 'ball speed vector'}
primitives.assumptions: Coverage efficiency scales inversely with E_g and directly with C_o.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When E_g > 0.1, game outcome shifts toward defensive failure.

layer2.mapping: Outfield positioning mirrors optimal control theory for minimizing spatial error in tracking moving targets.
layer2.telemetry: Distance covered per ground ball and time to intercept.

primitives.name: Infield Error Propagation
primitives.verbatim_quote: When a grounder is batted to an in-fielder and he makes an error, it usually results that all runners who are on the bases advance each one base.
primitives.assumptions: Each error triggers deterministic base advancement: A_b = R_n + 1.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At full bases (1st, 2nd, 3rd), error propagation maximizes.

layer2.mapping: Error propagation modeled as discrete-state Markov chain with absorbing states at home plate.
layer2.telemetry: Runner advancement frequency and base occupancy after infield errors.
